builder_plan.scenario: Long customer conversations exhaust memory or limit concurrent requests.
builder_plan.change: Change only the attention cache policy, after checking model and runtime support.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model with its ordinary attention cache.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak cache memory, long-context answer quality, first-token latency, and requests completed.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Runway Characters: Serving a 57B Video Diffusion Transformer for Real-Time Conversation
summary: The method recomputes whole-KV-cache work at write time (a ring cache with RoPE and FP8 quantization applied once per write, plus a delta rotation on position reset) instead of repeating it in every attention call, and fuses tensor-parallel all-reduce into the FP8 GEMM. It costs substantial engineering complexity: custom kernels, an in-switch reduction path that was rolled back once in production, and a four-GPU H100 topology with a dedicated decoder GPU. Failures include numerical risk from FP8 cache quantization (mitigated here by lip-sync validation but not guaranteed on other models), correctness bugs in the delta-rotation path, and fused-kernel instability under production load.
rationale: The write-time ring-cache principle is instructive, but the system targets a 57B model on four H100s with custom fused kernels, which is far outside a 24 GB single-GPU or API-based budget and cannot be adopted directly.
technique: Ring KV cache with write-time FP8/RoPE for video diffusion serving

claims.statement: The method recomputes whole-KV-cache work at write time (a ring cache with RoPE and FP8 quantization applied once per write, plus a delta rotation on position reset) instead of repeating it in every attention call, and fuses tensor-parallel all-reduce into the FP8 GEMM. It costs substantial engineering complexity: custom kernels, an in-switch reduction path that was rolled back once in production, and a four-GPU H100 topology with a dedicated decoder GPU. Failures include numerical risk from FP8 cache quantization (mitigated here by lip-sync validation but not guaranteed on other models), correctness bugs in the delta-rotation path, and fused-kernel instability under production load.
Cache and kernel optimizations cut the diffusion step from 240.9 to 159.3 ms (1.51x, 24.5 fps sustained); a fused FP8 all-reduce GEMM reaches 147.4 ms (1.63x), with no detected lip-sync degradation.
